ownership_reason: Only the gold iterates the entries of the supplied map, computes the position at which each mapping is put and decides where the next mapping goes; hops 1-4 pass the ordered map, the start index and the whole map along unchanged with one call each, so no one-line change above the gold can alter where the gold puts its second and later mappings (a different start index moves the whole block: one place later passes the trigger but puts the added mappings of testPutAllWithIndex one place too late). The gold's javadoc promises all the mappings put into the ordered map in the iteration order of the specified map, starting at the specified index, which [0, 1, 2, 4, 3] for the keys 0..4 of a TreeMap does not do. The convention is pinned outside the gold: the facade's own javadoc (the values put 'into the Map starting at the specified index'); ListOrderedMap.put(int, K, V), which moves a key that is already present to the given index (ListOrderedMapTest testPut_intObjectObject); ListOrderedSet.addAll(int, Collection), which inserts the elements at the index in their iteration order (ListOrderedSetTest testListAddIndexed); SetUniqueList.addAll(int, Collection); and consecutive placement in the supplied map's order from the start index, pinned by ListOrderedMapTest testPutAllWithIndex.
